assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational quantitative account of how allocative inefficiency shapes aggregate productivity and international income differences.
assessment.attribution: The three proposed laureates represent closely linked theoretical and empirical contributions; the boundaries with broader development and firm-dynamics literatures require careful framing.
assessment.maturity: The framework has had sustained influence across growth, development, and policy-oriented work.
uncertainties: Estimated misallocation and its welfare interpretation can depend materially on modeling and measurement assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed modern trade theory and empirical work on selection, productivity, and gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the core model, while Helpman and Redding are major contributors to its extensions and empirical integration.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is deeply embedded in trade research and has generated a large body of evidence.
uncertainties: A prize formulation would need to distinguish this contribution from adjacent heterogeneous-firm and quantitative-trade work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking structural analysis operational in a broad range of economic applications.
assessment.attribution: Rust provides the seminal methodological anchor, with Keane and Eckstein important contributors to estimation and applications.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been extensively used, tested, and developed over several decades.
uncertainties: The appropriate breadth of credit within the larger structural econometrics tradition is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods supplied widely influential tools for credible empirical work with persistent panel data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are especially inseparable from the core estimator, while Blundell is central to the system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding standards across applied microeconometrics and macroeconometrics.
uncertainties: Practical sensitivity to instruments and specification complicates assessment of the methods' empirical legacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and financial amplification provided an enduring mechanism connecting credit conditions to macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are central to the collateral-constraint mechanism; Gertler's work is central to its macroeconomic development.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism has become a core element of modern macro-finance and gained salience through repeated financial disruptions.
uncertainties: Credit-frictions research has many important contributors, making a bounded attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian modeling substantially changed analysis of monetary and fiscal transmission through household balance sheets.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan and Violante provide central foundations, with Moll a leading contributor to the quantitative heterogeneous-agent toolkit.
assessment.maturity: The approach is highly influential and increasingly incorporated into policy analysis.
uncertainties: Its relatively recent consolidation leaves less time to assess the durability of its central quantitative conclusions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work clarified how trade exposure and technological change reshape local labor markets, tasks, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the trade-shock contribution, while related work on technology broadens the attribution question.
assessment.maturity: The empirical findings have stimulated extensive replication, methodological development, and policy debate.
uncertainties: Local causal effects and their aggregate welfare implications need not coincide.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy analysis of institutions, state capacity, and fiscal policy has illuminated central determinants of long-run economic performance.
assessment.attribution: Besley and Persson provide a particularly integrated state-capacity program, while Tabellini has made major contributions on political institutions and culture.
assessment.maturity: The research has had durable influence across political economy, public finance, and development.
uncertainties: The broad field makes it challenging to identify a single discovery and a fully delimited set of laureates.
